game.title: Databases & SQL Fundamentals
game.description: A review of relational database basics: querying, joins, aggregation, keys, NULL semantics, transactions and indexes. Ends with three ungraded check-in questions for the instructor.

questions.prompt: Which SQL clause filters individual rows before they are grouped?
A column declared as a PRIMARY KEY may contain NULL values.
Which join returns every row from the left table, filling in NULLs where the right table has no match?
Which SQL keyword, placed right after SELECT, removes duplicate rows from the result?
Which of these are aggregate functions (they combine many rows into one value)? Select all that apply.
You want the number of customers in each city, but only for cities with more than 5 customers. Which query is best?

options: SELECT city, COUNT(*) FROM customers GROUP BY city HAVING COUNT(*) > 5
SELECT city, COUNT(*) FROM customers WHERE COUNT(*) > 5 GROUP BY city
SELECT city, COUNT(*) FROM customers GROUP BY city
SELECT city FROM customers WHERE city > 5

questions.prompt: In standard SQL, the condition NULL = NULL evaluates to TRUE.
In the ACID properties of a transaction, what does the A stand for?
What is the main job of a FOREIGN KEY constraint?

options: Making lookups on the column faster
Guaranteeing every value in the column is unique
Ensuring each value refers to an existing row in another table
Encrypting the column's values at rest

questions.prompt: Which statements belong to the Data Manipulation Language (DML), i.e. they change the rows stored in a table? Select all that apply.
Adding an index to a frequently searched column usually has which trade-off?

options: Faster reads, slower writes and more storage
No effect unless the column is a primary key

questions.prompt: Check-in (not graded for correctness): how confident are you writing a query that joins three tables?

options: I could do it with notes
